question: A food outlet sells two types of meal combos. The first combo contains 2 sandwiches and 1 juice and costs ₹80. The second combo contains 1 sandwich and 2 juices and costs ₹70. What is the price of one sandwich?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let sandwich = S, juice = J

2S + J = 80 and S + 2J = 70

Multiply second: 2S + 4J = 140

Subtract: (2S + 4J) − (2S + J) = 140 − 80 ⇒ 3J = 60 ⇒ J = 20

Put in S + 2J = 70 ⇒ S + 40 = 70 ⇒ S = 30

**∴ Answer = ₹30**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

2 sandwiches + 1 juice = 80, 1 sandwich + 2 juices = 70

**Formula used:**

Linear equations method

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let sandwich = S, juice = J

⇒ 2S + J = 80 ...(1)

⇒ S + 2J = 70 ...(2)

⇒ From (2): S = 70 − 2J

⇒ Substitute in (1): 2(70 − 2J) + J = 80

⇒ 140 − 4J + J = 80

⇒ 140 − 3J = 80

⇒ 3J = 60 ⇒ J = 20

⇒ S = 70 − 2(20) = 30

**∴ The correct answer is ₹30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations

Two equations with two variables can be solved using substitution or elimination method.

Elimination Method

Make coefficients same and subtract to eliminate one variable.

Substitution Method

Express one variable in terms of another and substitute.

Quick Check

Put values back: 2×30+20=80 and 30+40=70 ✔
